branches.pr_body:
## Summary
In S234, 5 of 14 T2 SEO metas ended in the middle of a phrase ("…mountain valleys with expert.") and 2 of 14 ended with the wrong country (", in Laos." on a Laos→Vietnam tour). Both come from the deterministic meta fit in `seo_meta_utils.py`, which A1 Master uses too. This PR fixes the fit itself and leaves the global sentence check without a noun/adjective heuristic, because `META_INCOMPLETE_SENTENCE` hard-blocks A1 Master and a noun ending has no deterministic fix.

The first commit is the A1 prompt golden-SHA guard. It was captured on main @20a2387 before any prompt edit, and AA-792 (stacked on this branch) builds on it.

## Changes
- `_cut_long_meta`: the last-resort word cut only cuts right before a word that opens a new phrase: and/with/across/through/while/… (not a/an/the/of/as). When no clean cut fits the band it returns None, so `SEO_META_TOO_LONG` stays and the existing flag_fix LLM meta repair (Haiku) rewrites the meta.
- `_extend_short_meta`: no `in <country>` tail when the tour name or the meta names another country (canonical names and 4+ letter aliases from `shared/country_resolver.COUNTRY_MASTER`). Days-only tails are still allowed.
- `meta_complete_sentence`: also rejects trailing articles and weak connectors (a, an, the, by, of, via, into, through, between, as). The fit already strips these, so the hard code keeps its deterministic repair.
- Fit facts now include `name` (`graph._apply_seo_meta_fit`, `flag_fix_node._apply_seo_fit_before_llm`).
- T3 (`tenant_pipeline.run_t3_qa_gate`) uses `fit_seo_meta_final`, the same fit the graph runs. Before, it used salvage only, so a length code could trigger a whole-tour rewrite.
- New log event `seo_meta_fit_unresolved` (reason, len) when the fit leaves a meta out of band. It counts the LLM fallbacks.
- `tests/unit/test_aa792_a1_prompt_golden.py`: pins the A1 system and user prompts as sha256. Covers the sync `generate_node` and Bedrock Batch `materialize_s1_prompt`, with and without a brand, plus the A1 nudge prompt.

## Tests
- New `tests/unit/test_aa794_seo_meta_cut_country.py` (20 cases): the 5 S234 fragments, the 2 wrong-country cases, the single-country regression, weak endings, T3 using the full fit, and `name` threading in graph and flag_fix.
- Still green: test_aa740 / aa747 / aa226 / aa724 / s218_hard_code_repair / aa231 / aa205 / aa201 / aa641 / aa639 / aa469.
- Full `pytest tests/unit tests/acp`: 3445 passed. flake8 (CI config) clean.

## Live verify
- Before merge: run the $0 read-only A1 sizing (`.tmp-session/s235/t2_rerun/a1_meta_sizing.py`, ECS exec SELECT). The number goes in `docs/implementation-notes/AA-794.md`. Any backfill is a separate issue.
- After deploy: confirm api and worker run the same SHA and the rollout is COMPLETED.
- Verified by the shared AA-792 T2 rerun (14 runs, $0 extra). All 14 seo_meta must be 140–155 chars and end in '.'. The scorer's cut-word detector must flag 0, and the 14 metas are listed for a human read. None of the 3 Laos→Vietnam versions may end with ', in Laos.'.

T2 is the tenant's own product, but its writer reused the A1 master prompt: "master content catalog", "never adopt a persona", a NEUTRAL register for every itinerary day, and the tenant brand only as an "append only" note. The itinerary length nudge then re-voiced days as Adventure Asia (130 nudges over the 14 S234 jobs). The T2 judge took min(brand_fit, distinct) with a mission cap of 6, while the profile has no mission field. Mission was judged absent on 72 of 104 calls, and none of those passed. S234 mean scores per tenant were 4.0–7.0, against 8.0 for A1.

Stacked on `fix/aa-794-t2-meta` (AA-794). Retarget to `main` after that PR merges.

The judge prompt, the scoring internals and the repeat-median are unchanged, so brand_fit stays comparable with S234.

- Integration: `test_compiled_graph_state_propagation.py` has a new T2 case. Brand fields reach the writer's system prompt and judge_score equals brand_fit. It ran green on a local Postgres test DB.

When `F4_seo_surface` was the only blocking failure, `sentence_repair.plan` returned `None`. Attempt 2 then paid for a full Sonnet `rewrite_with_feedback`, or the piece was held at attempt 2 because `last_try` reads `plan() is None`, so the attempt-3 SEO fit never ran. `plan` now returns `[]` for an F4-only ledger, the same as a title/meta-only F12. The loop then re-runs `_fit_seo_meta` and the gates on the unchanged text (`repair_mode: "seo_fields"`, $0 text cost). An F4 slug violation still takes the full rewrite, because the fit only folds the slug to ASCII and never writes a new one.

S234 evidence (124 pieces): 10 ledgers were F4-only. 3 of them took a full rewrite at attempt 1, 5 were held at attempt 2 without the attempt-3 fit, and 2 were at attempt 3.

## Changes
- `services/acp_content_writing/sentence_repair.py`: adds `_SLUG_PREFIXES` and `_slug_violation()`. The `[]` branch of `plan()` now fires for any SEO-field gate that is not a contract gate (F4 or a title/meta F12), unless an F4 violation names the slug. A contract gate alone (F16_faq / F14_first_line) still returns `None`, so it holds at once as before.
- `tests/unit/test_aa768_s234_hygiene.py`: the AA-768 assertion "F4 alone: unchanged (full rewrite)" is reversed on purpose (`[f4] -> []`).
- `tests/unit/test_aa776_f4_only_seo_fields.py` (new): plan cases (title/meta F4 -> `[]`; slug violations built through the real `gate_seo_surface` -> `None`; F4 + F3 -> `None`; F4 + F16 -> `[]`; F16 alone -> `None`), plus three service-loop tests with mocked writer and gates:
  - attempt-1 F4-only -> `seo_fields`, no rewrite and no repair call
  - attempt-2 F4-only is not `last_try`, so attempt 3 runs
  - slug-only F4 -> still a full rewrite
- `docs/implementation-notes/AA-776.md` (new). It records the reversal of the AA-768 "F4 alone keeps None" decision.

Behaviour change beyond the issue text:
- F4 + F16 used to return `None` and now returns `[]`, consistent with the existing SEO-only F12 + F16.
- SEO-only F12 + an F4 slug violation used to return `[]` and now returns `None`.

## Tests
- `pytest tests/unit tests/acp`: 3414 + 14 passed, no DB.
- The new tests fail on main: 8/14 red without the fix.
- flake8 with the CI flags is clean on the touched service file.
- Integration tests were not run (no local DB). Only `plan()` and its unit tests changed.

## Live verify
After Deploy Dev reaches COMPLETED on both `aa-cis-dev-api` and `aa-cis-dev-worker` at the same SHA (`t9_write` runs on the worker): in the r5 checkpoint, every `repair_log` entry whose blocking failures are only `F4_seo_surface` must be followed by `repair_mode: "seo_fields"` (GET `/admin/content-quality/pieces/{id}`). If r5 produces no F4-only ledger, close on the unit tests plus the absence of an F4-only full rewrite. Do not pay for a run just for this.

## Summary
S234 gate evaluation (80 pieces vs the panel) found that every T9 `F1_grounding` violation was a year format and none was a real invented number:
- `'38'` read out of "1637–38"
- `'1630'` out of "the late 1630s"
- `'1990'` out of "since the early 1990s" (the seed says "established in 1992")

`find_novel_numeric_claims` gains an opt-in, keyword-only `year_forms: bool = False`. Only the T9/T10 `quality_gates.gate_grounding` passes `True`, which also covers the AA-769 admin sentence check because it calls the same gate. T3, A1 and source_facts call the function without the keyword, so their behaviour is byte-identical. F1 stays blocking: the interim "warn until fixed" step in the issue is dropped because the tolerance ships in this PR.

Rules when `year_forms=True`:
- **Range** `YYYY–YY` / `YYYY-YY` / `YYYY—YY` / `YYYY/YY`:
  - The start year is checked like any number.
  - The tail is expanded to the full year, rolling over the century when needed (`1998–02` → 2002).
  - The end year is supported when the seed has it (a seed range `1637–52` counts as 1652), or when it is start + 1 and the seed has the start.
  - Otherwise the FULL end year is reported (`'1652'`, not `'52'`).
- **Decade** `YYY0s` / `YYY0's`: supported by any seed year inside the decade. `YY00s` ("the 1600s") is read as the century. Otherwise it is reported as `'1880s'`.
- Every other number is checked exactly as before. The violation message format is unchanged, so `sentence_repair._F1_QUOTE_RE` still parses it.

## Changes
- `services/acp_shared/grounding.py`: adds `_YEAR_RANGE_RE`, `_DECADE_RE`, `_range_years`, `_decade_supported` and `_novel_year_forms`, plus the `year_forms` keyword. The default path is untouched.
- `services/acp_content_writing/quality_gates.py`: `gate_grounding` passes `year_forms=True`.
- `tests/unit/test_aa785_f1_year_forms.py` (new):
  - the S234 sentences as fixtures, with their real seed lines
  - negatives: `1637–52` → 1652; `1880s`; `1990s` without a 199x year; `38 km`; `1500–20 m` → 1520
  - default-off parity, including the AA-325 79-unit fixture under both readings
  - gate wiring, and a round-trip through `_F1_QUOTE_RE` / `sentence_repair.plan`
- `tests/unit/test_aa768_s234_round3.py`: two tests used "the late 1630s" against a seed containing 1637 as their F1 example, which is exactly the false positive this PR removes. Their seed no longer has a 163x year, so the sentence is still flagged (`['1630s']`) and the tests keep their intent.
- `tests/unit/test_aa298_aa325_grounding.py`: unchanged and green.
- `docs/implementation-notes/AA-785.md` (new).

## Tests
- `pytest tests/unit tests/acp`: 3460 passed, no DB.
- flake8 with the CI flags is clean on the touched service files.
- Offline replay (`.tmp-session/s235/aa785_replay.py`, $0, no LLM) over the 80 S234 pieces and 145 stored texts (final plus discarded attempts): the plain reading gives 10 F1 violations, all of them year forms; the `year_forms` reading gives 0. 0 violations were added and 0 non-year results changed.
- The plain-reading replay matches the stored ledgers on 143/145 texts. The 2 differences are the same `'1990'` quoted from a different sentence chunk.
- The remaining stored ledger strings come from attempt texts that were repaired and are not stored. Their sentences are unit-test fixtures.

After Deploy Dev reaches COMPLETED on api + worker at the same SHA (no `shared.job` queued or running at merge), run the same script with `--db` inside the worker container (S3-mediated ECS exec). It does one read-only SELECT of `acp_shared.content_piece` (writer_input, content_text, discarded_attempts, gate_ledger) for the 80 ids and rebuilds the exact grounding with `service.grounding_from_writer_input`. Expected: `new_year_form_f1: 0`, `added: []`, `other_changed: []`. Paste the output into the Linear comment.

branches.pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes the /admin/tenants bugs found in the S234 audit. The Active toggle returned 200 and changed nothing. New tenants got no `plan_id`, so quota and price showed 0/inf. Delete was an unaudited soft delete that left the key valid. Tenant writes were not audited. `GET /admin/tenants/{id}/usage` returned 500 for every tenant.

Gate-1 defaults applied (still to be confirmed by Nghiep):
- There are three states: active, suspended and offboarded.
- Suspend and resume are reversible.
- Offboarded is terminal. There is no restore route, and PATCH and generate-key return 409.
- Offboard cancels the tenant's QUEUED jobs. Running jobs are not touched.
- Tenant writes are admin-role only.
- GDPR data deletion is a follow-up.

The plan_id backfill was already done in S234 and is not repeated here.

## Changes

**Backend: `api/routers/admin.py`**
- `PATCH /admin/tenants/{id}` now takes a JSON body `UpdateTenantRequest {plan_tier?, is_active?}`. An empty body returns 422.
  - A plan change updates `plan_tier`, `plan_id` and `rate_limit_rpm` together.
  - On an offboarded tenant it returns 409.
  - Each change writes an audit row with before/after in the same transaction. It then drops the Redis `tenant_meta:{id}` cache so a suspend takes effect at once instead of after up to 30 s.
- `POST /admin/tenants` resolves `plan_id` from `shared.membership_plans` (active row for the tier). A tier with no active plan row returns 400 rather than storing NULL.
- `GET /admin/tenants` gets an opt-in `include_inactive` flag. The default stays active-only for atom-curation, tenant-activity and the command palette. Each row now carries a derived `status` and `cancelled_at`.
- `GET /admin/tenants/{id}/usage`:
  - The monthly series now comes from `shared.tenant_api_usage`. The old query read migration-007 column names from `shared.v_tenant_monthly_usage`, which the live view no longer has. The view itself is AA-798.
  - The tours quota is read by `plan_id`.
  - `tours_published`, which was always 0, is replaced by `t2_versions` and `t2_tours`.
- `POST /admin/tenants/{id}/generate-key` returns 409 for an offboarded tenant and writes an audit row.
- `PUT .../brand-identity` and `PUT .../config` each write an audit row. The config row holds before/after.
- `POST /admin/tenants/{id}/offboard`:
  - Cancels the tenant's queued `shared.job` rows, matched on `payload->>'tenant_id'` with `status='queued'`, then runs each kind's `on_terminal` hook. This is the same follow-up as the job-runner cancel route.
  - Refuses the AA internal tenant.
  - Uses the real admin as actor.
  - Drops the stale acc1 `acp-cis-bronze-867490540162` note.
- The bare `DELETE /admin/tenants/{id}` route is removed.
- Every tenant write requires `x-admin-role: admin`. The BFF always forwards it. The audit actor is `admin:{x-admin-user-id}`.

**`services/acp_shared/audit_log.py`**: new `AdminTenantAuditAction` constants. `agency.onboard` and `agency.offboard` keep their action strings.

**`frontend/app/admin/tenants/page.tsx`** (minimal, since AA-766 rebuilds this page):
- Loads with `?include_inactive=true`.
- The status chip shows Active/Suspended/Offboarded. It is disabled for offboarded rows.
- New status filter.
- Summary cards: Active, Suspended, Offboarded and Master.
- Delete is replaced by Offboard: a kit Modal with a required reason.

### Tenant lifecycle (AA-797)
A tenant (`shared.tenants`) is in one of three states, derived from two columns:
- **active**: `is_active = true`, `cancelled_at IS NULL`.
- **suspended**: `is_active = false`, `cancelled_at IS NULL`. Reversible through `PATCH /admin/tenants/{id} {"is_active": ...}`. The rate-limit middleware returns 403 "Tenant is deactivated" to the tenant's JWT. The PATCH clears the 30 s Redis `tenant_meta:{id}` cache, so this applies at once.
- **offboarded**: `cancelled_at` set. Reached only through `POST /admin/tenants/{id}/offboard`, which needs a reason. That call revokes the key (`api_key_hash = 'REVOKED_' || id`), sets `is_active = false`, removes the tenant from the Jev allow-list and cancels its QUEUED `shared.job` rows (running jobs finish).

Offboarded is terminal: PATCH and generate-key return 409, and no restore route exists. GDPR data deletion is not automated (follow-up).

Every admin write to a tenant (create, plan, status, key, brand identity, config, offboard) is admin-role only. The BFF enforces this through `lib/rbac.ts` `API_WRITE_RULES`, and the backend re-checks `x-admin-role`. Each write leaves one `acp_shared.audit_log` row (`AdminTenantAuditAction`, actor `admin:{x-admin-user-id}`). `plan_id` (-> `shared.membership_plans`) is set on create and on every plan change. `GET /admin/tenants` lists only active tenants unless `include_inactive=true`.
